record.original_question: Which 3-regular graphs G occur as the underlying graph of a closed geodesic net on the round 3-sphere? Here a closed geodesic net is a geodesic net with no unbalanced vertices.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.0.2. Classify all 3-regular graphs G such that the round 3-sphere has a geodesic net modelled on G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A geodesic net in a Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is a finite graph $G=(V,E)$ together with a continuous map from $G$ to $M$ that sends each edge to a (nonconstant) geodesic segment of $M$. At each vertex $v\in V$, let $\tau_1(v),\dots,\tau_{\deg(v)}(v)\in T_{f(v)}M$ denote the unit tangent vectors to the outgoing edge geodesics. The vertex $v$ is called balanced if $\sum_{i=1}^{\deg(v)}\tau_i(v)=0$. A closed geodesic net is a geodesic net in which every vertex is balanced (no unbalanced vertices).

Let $S^3$ denote the round $3$-sphere, equipped with its standard constant-curvature-$1$ metric. Classify all $3$-regular (finite, simple or multi-) graphs $G$ that arise as the underlying graph of some closed geodesic net realized in $S^3$. That is, determine exactly which $3$-regular graphs $G$ admit a continuous map $f:G\to S^3$ sending each edge to a geodesic arc such that at every vertex the three unit tangent vectors to the outgoing edges sum to zero.
artifact.status_search_result: A search reveals work classifying 3-regular geodesic nets on the round 2-sphere (Heppes' classical list) and on flat doubled polygons, but no source claims a classification of 3-regular closed geodesic nets on the round 3-sphere. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic nets on flat spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Classification results are obtained for 3-regular geodesic nets on flat doubled polygons; no analogous classification on the round 3-sphere is given.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses 3-regular geodesic nets in 2D settings, not on the round 3-sphere.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic nets on the 2-sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Heppes classified geodesic nets with degree-three vertices on the round 2-sphere into ten types.
status_evidence.claim: On the round 2-sphere the analogous classification is known (Heppes), but the 3-sphere case is not addressed.
